newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: U.S. Marines complete Sierra Leone airlift.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Marines complete Sierra Leone airlift.

text.p: American marines on Friday completed an airlift of U.S. citizens and other Westerners fleeing a violent coup in Sierra Leone, marine officers said.
A squadron of 15 helicopters ferried 900 people, including 300 Americans, from a hotel in the capital Freetown to the U.S. warship Kearsarge lying 12 miles offshore.

A rush of frightened foreigners scrambling to leave before an expected strike by a Nigerian-led regional military force against the coup leaders pushed the number evacuated to double what was estimated.
The last civilian passenger airlifted from the grounds of the Mammy Yoko hotel was a young Lebanese housewife in the early stages of labour.
Doctors said they expected the baby to be delivered later on Friday night on the Kearsarge, which is expected to dock in Conakry, Guinea in two days.
